# caliper-docgen: new session (2026-10-31)

You are working on caliper-docgen (github.com/orin-dx/caliper): a Rust/OXC React props extractor. The product is accurate AND fast Storybook docs, and agents via `monokl` use it in-process (no shell-out). It should beat react-docgen-typescript (RDT) on speed and match it on accuracy, and be competitive with react-docgen.

## Your task: close the v1 alpha gap = accuracy gaps + TS 7.1 on-demand work

Start by reading docs/STATUS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/architecture/, docs/measurement.md, docs/adr/README.md and AGENTS.md. Then restate the definition of done below to the user and get a yes before you build.

Definition of done (agree on numbers using step 1's baseline):
- Recall vs RDT with TS 7.1 off: shadcn and antd close to Mantine/Chakra/Spectrum (those are 98.6-99.7% of props with dependencies loaded). Report own props and @types/react props separately.
- Dropped syntax is kept: readonly, index signatures, RefObject, each with an exact-prop-set test, in ONE schema bump (v4).
- On-demand TS 7.1 is safe to ship as an experimental opt-in: version range plus self-check, bounded memory, no startup stall, and a real-tsc test running in CI. Promotion past experimental is out of scope until TS 7.1 is stable and the oracle wrong-rate stays near 0%.

Order:
1. Baseline: run the weekly workflow by hand (workflow_dispatch on weekly.yml). Record per-corpus recall, time, peak RSS and oracle wrong-rate. Every later change is judged against it.
2. Schema v4 batch FIRST, one PR: readonly, index signatures, RefObject, with exact-prop-set tests. Bump SCHEMA_VERSION once, update docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md, and write a changeset in consumer terms (what must be updated together). ADR 0017 is the versioning rule.
3. Root-cause the shadcn and antd recall gap BEFORE building: diff caliper against RDT per missing prop and group by cause (ComponentProps<typeof X> of dependencies, Radix/base-ui wrappers, Omit/Pick chains, polymorphic generics; antd PurePanel's 33 props may be a harness pairing bug). Fix by shape, never by library name. Any fix that changes the JSON must not bump the version again. Each fix gets an exact-content test and a bench check (time AND peak RSS).
4. Detection by shape: memo(forwardRef(function...)) without type arguments; React APIs (forwardRef, memo, createContext) matched by import source instead of name; the {Name}Props naming heuristic in tagged-factory becomes a shape rule; Chakra NonNullable<union> reduction.
5. On-demand hardening (crates/semantic, crates/tsc-client, ADR 0022): version range plus self-check against the installed typescript (it is pinned to the exact 7.1.0-beta today); a memory cap for the tsc process (157-612 MiB observed); a disk cache and prefetch only if numbers justify them; enable the real-tsc test in CI (skipped today). Re-measure first-story latency (82-137 ms, Chakra 703) and later-story latency (21-41 ms).
6. Re-run the weekly workflow, compare with step 1, and update docs/STATUS.md and the numbers on the site.

If a gap only closes with the TS checker, say so in its trail instead of forcing it into the structural resolver.

Trails: create one per goal with acceptance criteria BEFORE any branch: (a) recall gaps shadcn/antd, (b) schema v4 dropped syntax, (c) detection by shape, (d) on-demand hardening. Name each by the area of work, succinct and friendly. Link each branch with `entire trail link <n> --project gh/orin-dx --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper --branch <branch>` BEFORE `gh pr create` (Entire opens a draft PR when you link; fill that one in and mark it ready, don't open a second). Do not approve trails yourself.

## Current state
- main is green. All of last week's stack merged (#229-#264). The release PR #239 (0.7.0 to 0.8.0, the first release on Callisto 0.16.0, schema v3) is being released by the user now. Schema v4 ships in the release after it, so the v4 changeset must carry the migration note.
- The tap (orin-dx/homebrew-tap) pulls from our tags (npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z) with brew bump and builds crates/cli from source. We push nothing.
- Shipped recently: lazy sessions, full HTML-attribute default (curated is opt-in), TS 7.1 on-demand (semanticTypes: 'on-demand', experimental, off by default), tagged-factory and forwardRef-by-shape detection, intersection reads, function optional/rest params, OXC 0.155, Callisto 0.16.0.
- Measurement is now ONE weekly workflow (scripts/weekly.py: caliper vs RDT vs react-docgen plus the TS oracle, artifacts, one issue on regression) and `just bench [branch]` (local A/B vs origin/main, median of 9). The PR gates (Equivalence, Parity, Scorecard, allow-list) were deleted. Do not rebuild them.
- Earlier numbers (one machine, not the pinned run): 22-67x faster than RDT and 3.8-9.5x less memory; 17-43x faster than react-docgen on shadcn/antd/Mantine/Spectrum (Chakra only about 4x); @types/react recall 92-99% with full. Treat them as stale until the step-1 baseline exists.
- ADRs only for architecture. Kept: 0001, 0002, 0003, 0005, 0006, 0007, 0009, 0010, 0016, 0017, 0018, 0022. The others are retired with tombstones in docs/adr/README.md.

## Rules (they cost us real incidents)
- Commits MUST be GPG-signed: main requires signatures, a merge queue and 1 approving review, and blocks non-fast-forward. Run git with the sandbox OFF, never use --no-gpg-sign, and check `git log -1 --format='%h %G?'` shows G.
- Never force-push, never merge PRs, never push to main. The user merges, with MERGE COMMITS only (squash and rebase are off). main was force-pushed backwards once and lost about 295 commits; verify main's tip before assuming anything.
- Prefer independent PRs off main, small, with new tests in new files. Entire "stacks" cannot be retargeted after the parent merges. Stack only when a PR truly depends on an unmerged one, and say so in the body.
- Forks and parallel agents need `isolation: "worktree"`; two agents in one worktree clobber each other.
- git here: use /usr/bin/git, one plain git command per call; other worktrees can only be inspected through a python subprocess. Don't pipe lint or test output into tail or head; read the exit code directly.
- AGENTS.md rules: no unwrap outside tests, FxHashMap internally and BTreeMap for JSON, CompactString for names, no AST refs escape parse_file, emit a Diagnostic whenever you degrade. Add sibling-path parity tests and assert exact content, not presence.
- Writing: succinct, friendly, no hard-wrapping. A changeset is one short consumer-facing paragraph that starts with the outcome (read AGENTS.md). Commits: imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why. Commits end with `Claude-Session: <session url>`; PR bodies end with the session url.
- Measure time AND peak RSS for any resolver change (`just bench`, the weekly job). Calibrated noise: wall 1.10x and RSS 1.20x, median of 9 interleaved runs.
- Keep it simple. The user rejected heavy gate machinery ("you're shaving a yak"). Prefer small, boring, reliable.
- Closing, retargeting or deleting other people's PRs, branches and trails is the user's call: list them, don't do them.

## Useful
- Tools: `just lint doc-check typos`, `cargo nextest run -p cabench`, scripts/weekly.py, apps/oracle (the TS 7.1 oracle),packages/storybook/scripts/storybook-parity.mjs (build napi first), corpus pins in scripts/corpora.py.
- Entire Gates needs a human approval on each trail; that is t

## Housekeeping the user owns
- Delete the remote branches `scratch/gate-calibration` and `scratch/parity-allow-probe`, plus merged and old scratch branches.
- Delete TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID and TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY from calipeey are set here.
- Close stale Entire trails.

1	# Status
2	
3	**Updated:** 2026-10-22
4	
5	Core extraction, resolver, CLI, NAPI binding, and Vite plugin all work and are fully tested. Config file loading, watch mode (including rebuilds on config changes and polling with `ensure_fresh`), plugin architecture, TOON token-optimized output format, JSON schema export, and bounded atomic DTS caching are implemented and verified.
6	
7	**Types from other packages.** Imports resolve to any file under a source directory, `.d.ts` included, so a monorepo whose packages are all source directories resolves across them. By default the declarations those names point to are loaded (ADR 0010, on by default since ADR 0019): a prop typed by an installed package resolves. `--no-load-dependencies` (config, NAPI and Vite `loadDependencies: false`) reads only `@types/react` and TypeScript's own lib files from `node_modules`, and then a prop whose type comes from any other installed package stays a named reference with an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` warning. Checked against RDT on five installed repos, loading reports far more of RDT's props and changes 11 matching types in 59,000. Chakra, the worst case, costs about 220 ms and 330 MiB against 50 ms and 100 MiB without (`docs/performance.md`).
8	
9	## Numbers
10	
11	- Rust tests (`cargo nextest` across the workspace, plus the NAPI binding tests) and vitest (unit with a mocked binding, integration against the real native binding), all green in CI
12	- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean with `unsafe_code = "deny"` enforced workspace-wide
13	- 20 real-world fixture libraries validated against `react-docgen-typescript` (shadcn, Radix, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, antd, ariakit, ark-ui, base-ui, blueprint, day-picker, fluentui, headlessui, panda, react-final-form, react-resizable-panels, storybook-emotion, tanstack-table, zendesk-garden — see `rdt-coverage.md`)
14	- **Recall** against `react-docgen-typescript` with dependencies installed and loaded (`docs/parity.md`, 2026-10-23): share of RDT's non-React props reported Mantine 99.7%, Chakra 98.6%, shadcn/ui 39.5%, Ant Design 80.3%, react-spectrum 99.7%.
15	- **Precision** per detection rule (`docs/precision.md`, 2026-10-21): 1 component that isn't one in 154 sampled, `functionDeclaration` 96% and every other rule 100%. 25 samples per rule can't yet establish the 95% gate.
16	- **Speed** on five pinned public corpora (`docs/performance.md`, 2026-10-22): 34 to 81 ms wall time and 66 to 153 MB peak RSS for 41 to 490 kLOC, 17 to 39 times faster than `react-docgen-typescript` on the same files. CI fails on a 10% regression against main or a ratio under 10×.
17	
18	## Features and improvements
19	
20	- **`htmlAttributes` defaults to `full`** (ADR 0024) — every attribute `@types/react` declares is listed, `ref` for `forwardRef` and `ComponentProps<"div">` props; `curated` is an opt-in compact mode. Costs against the old default: wall time +9 to +31%, peak RSS +12 to +37%, canonical JSON +42 to +105%.
21	- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
22	- **Plugin system** (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) — Extensible AST and component resolution hooks in `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`.
23	- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
24	- **JSON schema export** (`caliper-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
25	- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap.
26	- **Strict Safe Rust** — `unsafe_code = "deny"` via `[workspace.lints]`, active across all three crates (`core`, `cli`, `binding`) — none currently use `unsafe`, including the NAPI FFI boundary (napi-rs's `#[napi]` macros generate the glue without user-visible `unsafe`).
27	
28	## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker
29	
30	See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types that need inference (`infer`, an unbound generic), mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs. A conditional, indexed access or mapped type whose operands are known is evaluated (`resolver/evaluate.rs`).
31	
32	An opt-in TypeScript 7 semantic backend is implemented as slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007), experimental and off by default: `extract --experimental-semantic-types`, see `type-checker-integration.md`. Accuracy is verified against real RDT — 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and re-verified on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches; the gap is explained noise, not a resolver bug) — and the RDT oracle that comparison depends on now runs on its own `typescript@6` install, separate from the semantic probe's `typescript@7.1.0-beta`. TypeScript 7.1's checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/parity.md`). A missing, crashed or timed-out `tsc` falls back to the structural result with one warning; the open lifecycle items are in `type-checker-integration.md`'s Gates table.
33	
34	## Experiments that didn't pan out
35	
36	**Confidence routing (2026-10-25).** The idea: score each component's risk of wrong or missing props from Caliper's own output, and ask the TypeScript 7.1 checker only about the risky ones. Measured against the checker on 518,268 shared props over the five corpora and the fixtures, routing 10% of components caught 23% of the props only the checker reports with the existing warning rule (a component with a degrade warning or error), against 3% for a smoothed table and 6% for a logistic model. At a 20% budget neither model caught the one prop the oracle marks `wrong`. Most of the checker-only props were Next's ambient augmentation (1,154 of 1,182 on shadcn) or false component matches, which a score of structural risk can't learn. So no score ships: warnings stay the signal, and on-demand checker use asks about the requested component instead of predicting. The script was deleted; the method is `scripts/parity.py oracle` plus the numbers above.
37	
38	## Where to look next
39	
40	- **Open gaps** → `edge-cases.md` — the gaps still open. Add one when you find a gap you aren't fixing now; delete it when you fix it.
41	- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
42	- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, panic containment, the TypeScript 7 semantic backend. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
43	- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (moved from `.claude/semantic-model/` so every coding agent can read it, not just Claude Code — `AGENTS.md` is now this repo's shared instructions file, with per-tool mirrors under `.codex/`, `.cursor/`, `.gemini/`, `.github/`, `.opencode/`).
44	- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
45	- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`

1	# caliper-docgen
2	
3	10-100x faster than react-docgen-typescript. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON via `--format rdt`. See `docs/STATUS.md` for current state and known gaps.
4	
5	## Commands
6	
7	```bash
8	cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core          # unit + snapshot tests
9	cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
10	cargo build --release                         # full build including CLI
11	```
12	
13	Or use `/check` and `/snapshot` for the common workflows.
14	
15	## Non-negotiables
16	
17	1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
18	2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps
19	3. `CompactString` for type/prop names in hot paths
20	4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()` — allocator is local per call
21	5. No terminal/display code in `crates/core`
22	6. Always emit `Diagnostic` when degrading — never fail silently
23	
24	## Architecture
25	
26	```
27	OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
28	```
29	
30	No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).
31	
32	See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full pipeline/crate-graph overview, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (pipeline orchestration, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, CLI, NAPI binding) — start at `docs/architecture/README.md`.
33	
34	## Decisions
35	
36	Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.
37	
38	## Testing discipline
39	
40	Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):
41	
42	1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
43	2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.
44	
45	## Crate guide
46	
47	- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
48	- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
49	- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core
50	
51	## Writing and commits
52	
53	- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in `docs/adr/README.md`.
54	- Changesets become bullets under generated changelog headings. Write one short, consumer-facing paragraph per changeset; start with the outcome, and include an upgrade action or cost when needed. Do not start the body with a heading or list marker.
55	- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions: one line per paragraph.
56	- Comments: only the non-obvious why, no history (the commit records it). Fill to 120 columns (`.rustfmt.toml`). Rewriting a comment block counts as writing it: re-fill and cut it, don't inherit the old wrapping.
57	- Commits: imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why, no list of what changed, no "This commit...". Skip the body when the subject says it all.
58

60	Read .entire/agent-guide.md for this repository's workflow, source inspection, and verification guidance.
61	@.entire/agent-guide.md
62	<!-- entire-agent:end -->

1	# Architecture Decision Records
2	
3	Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.
4	
5	## Index
6	
7	One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.
8	
9	- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — do not add a type-checking pass to the default path. The opt-in backend is 0006.
10	- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
11	- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
12	- 4. Defer full type-checker integration — removed: superseded by 0006. The gap list and gates are in `docs/type-checker-integration.md`.
13	- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
14	- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.
15	
16	- [7. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default](0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md) — do not feature-gate the backend crate, run it by default, or let it replace a structural entry on a clash.
17	- [8. Discard the parse cache whenever the build that wrote it differs](0008-parse-cache-keyed-by-build.md) — do not load cache entries without checking the payload's header against the running build.
18	- [9. Write each distinct prop once in the canonical output](0009-canonical-output-interns-props.md) — do not inline props in canonical JSON or derive prop ids from position.
19	- [10. Load dependency declarations by name, before resolution, into a shared layer](0010-load-dependency-declarations-by-name.md) — do not load dependency files by import closure, resolve against them lazily during resolution, or emit their components or enums. Its precedence of shortcuts over dependency declarations is superseded by 0014.
20	- [11. Find dependency declarations through a per-package export index, not the parse cache](0011-per-package-export-index.md) — do not put dependency files in the `DtsCache` or reuse an index whose package's `package.json` changed.
21	- [12. Collapse large inherited dependency sources, as Storybook does](0012-collapse-large-dependency-sources.md) — do not resolve a collapsed source's props, or collapse a component's own props.
22	- [13. Read React's attribute declarations in curated mode, in an index of their own](0013-curated-mode-reads-react-attributes-apart.md) — do not merge React into the project index outside Full mode, or make the React index a lookup fallback.
23	- [14. A loaded declaration wins over a known shortcut; shortcuts are fallbacks](0014-declarations-before-shortcuts.md) — do not check a shortcut before a declaration, or add one without measuring it against the declaration on consumer code.
24	- 15. A member read through React's types reads React's declaration and what it imports — removed: a resolver behavior, not a structure. It lives in `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md` ("Member reads through React's types").
25	- [16. Resolve components on request, and load dependencies for the names their resolution reaches](0016-resolve-components-on-request.md) — do not make a lazy answer differ from batch extraction's for the same key, memoize a resolution that found a dependency name missing, or expose a parser type from the session API. Extends 0010's loading from "before resolution" to "before the resolution that answers".
26	- [17. Version the canonical JSON, and make readers reject a version they don't read](0017-version-the-canonical-json.md) — do not change the canonical JSON's shape without bumping `SCHEMA_VERSION`, or let a reader accept a version it was not written for.
27	- [18. Write prop sets and name lists once in the canonical output](0018-canonical-output-interns-prop-sets-and-name-lists.md) — do not write a component's props, an inheritance layer's `omitted` or a diagnostic's `affects` inline in canonical JSON. Extends 0009's per-prop table to the lists that repeat across components; `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2.
28	- [19. Load dependency declarations by default](0019-load-dependencies-by-default.md) — do not make a surface default `loadDependencies` to off, or compare a baseline recorded without a flag against a build with the other default. Supersedes 0010's "off by default".
29	- 20. Chain dependency layers and load the remaining names after three growths — removed: a tuning of 0016's design with measurements, not a new decision. It lives in `docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md` ("Demand-driven dependencies") and `docs/performance.md`. It replaced 0016's 48-growth threshold.
30	- [21. Publish the semantic backend crates with the CLI](0021-publish-the-semantic-backend-crates.md) — keep the runtime opt-in backend available in the published CLI by releasing its versioned crate dependencies first.
31	- [22. Ask a warm checker for the requested component](0022-ask-a-warm-checker-for-the-requested-component.md) — do not route by predicted risk or check the whole project to answer one story: ask the TypeScript checker for the component a request names, wait a bounded time, and take the structural answer when it is slower. Extends 0007's runtime opt-in from a project run to a session.
32	- [23. Function parameters carry `optional` and `rest`](0023-function-parameters-carry-optional-and-rest.md) — do not print a function type without its `?` and `...` parameters, or add a parameter flag without a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and a reader update. `SCHEMA_VERSION` 3.
33	- [24. List every HTML attribute React declares by default](0024-list-every-html-attribute-by-default.md) — do not make `curated` the default `htmlAttributes`, or omit a prop `@types/react` declares. Supersedes 0013's default
34	
35	Changing any of these needs a new ADR. A removed entry keeps its number; its rationale moved to the doc named on its line.
36	
37	## When to write one
38	
39	Two gates, both required:
40	
41	1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
42	2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?
43	
44	If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.
45	
46	Good candidates:
47	
48	- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
49	- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
50	- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned
51	
52	Not ADR material:
53	
54	- A default, threshold or resolution order that one module reads (a collapse limit, a growth count, which lookup goes first) — that's a code comment plus the subsystem's `docs/architecture/` page. Measurements belong in `docs/performance.md`.
55	- A release or CI procedure (what to publish first, which gate blocks) — that's the workflow file.
56	- A superseded or tuned earlier decision whose design still holds — update the architecture page, don't stack a new ADR on it. Write one only if the contract itself changes.
57	- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
58	- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
59	- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
60	- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
61	- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
62	- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory
63	
64	## Format
65	
66	One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.
67	
68	- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
69	- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
70	- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.
71	
72	## Writing it
73	
74	Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.
75	
76	**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.
77	
78	| Instead of | Write |
79	| --- | --- |
80	| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
81	| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
82	| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
83	| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |
84	
85	**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.
86	
87	**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.
88	
89	**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.
90	
91	**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.
92	
93	**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.
94	
95	## What good looks like
96	
97	Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.

1	# 0017. Version the canonical JSON, and make readers reject a version they don't read
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-24
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	The canonical JSON has changed shape under its readers once already: ADR 0009 replaced inline props with ids, and nothing told a reader of the old shape. Three packages parse it (`caliper-docgen-napi`'s types, the Vite plugin, the Storybook addon), and so will other tools, such as an agent server linking `caliper-docgen-core`. Semver on the packages and changesets does not guard the JSON: a reader and the binding can be installed at different releases, and the mismatch surfaces as `undefined is not iterable` somewhere downstream.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	Every canonical JSON document carries `schemaVersion`, an integer: `ExtractionOutput` (CLI `--json` and `--format canonical`, NAPI `extractAll`, `initializeSession`), `IncrementalUpdate`, and the session index (`initializeSessionIndex`). `SCHEMA_VERSION` in `crates/core/src/types/output.rs` is the one definition. The shape ADR 0009 describes is version 1.
12	
13	- **Bump** when a reader of the previous version would misread or lose data: a field removed, renamed or retyped, a field's meaning changed, or references and tables restructured.
14	- **Don't bump** for additions a reader can ignore: a new field, a new `detectedBy` value, a new diagnostic code. Readers must tolerate those.
15	- **Readers** accept their own version and reject any other with an error naming both versions. Output with no `schemaVersion` predates it and has version 1's shape.
16	- **Release:** a bump goes out in a changeset marked breaking for the core crate and every package that reads the JSON, so writer and readers move together.
17	- `--format rdt`, `--format storybook` and `--format toon` have other tools' shapes and carry no version. The parse cache has its own `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
18	
19	## Consequences
20	
21	- A mismatched install fails at the first read with a message that says what to update, instead of a type error deep in a consumer.
22	- Every shape change needs a deliberate bump, a changeset and a reader update. That is the point, and it costs a small coordinated release each time.
23	- An old reader cannot read new output at all, even the parts that didn't change. We accept that over a reader that half-works.
24	- `ExtractionOutput`'s `Deserialize` rejects a version other than `SCHEMA_VERSION`. Reading older versions would need a migration per version, which nothing needs today.
25	
26	## Alternatives considered
27	
28	- **Semver of the package as the contract:** readers and the binding are separate installs, so the package version does not say which shape a document has.
29	- **A range or a minor version in the document:** none of the three readers can use a "compatible up to" statement, and the "don't bump" rule already covers compatible additions.
30

input.command:
python3 -I - <<'E'
import subprocess as s
g=lambda *a:s.run(["/usr/bin/git",*a],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
print("main",g("rev-parse","--short","main").strip(),"origin",g("rev-parse","--short","origin/main").strip())
merged=set(x.strip("* +") for x in g("branch","--merged","origin/main","--format=%(refname:short)").split())
wts={}
cur=None
for l in g("worktree","list","--porcelain").splitlines():
    if l.startswith("worktree "):cur=l[9:]
    if l.startswith("branch "):wts[l[18:]]=cur
for l in g("branch","--format=%(refname:short)|%(upstream:track)|%(committerdate:short)").splitlines():
    n,t,d=l.split("|")
    if n=="main":continue
    print(("M" if n in merged else "-"),("G" if "gone" in t else "-"),("W" if n in wts else "-"),d,n)
E

name: Weekly

# Caliper, react-docgen-typescript and react-docgen on five public repos with their dependencies installed: time,
# memory and recall (docs/measurement.md). It compares with last week's record and opens or updates one issue when
# Caliper got slower, bigger or less complete. It never runs on a pull request and never fails one.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"

jobs:
  weekly:
    name: Weekly
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      # The corpora's own package managers run under Node 24: Yarn 4.18, which Mantine and React Spectrum pin, crashes
      # under the repository's Node 26 ("Dynamic require of "util" is not supported"). This step comes before the
      # toolchain's so that the toolchain's Node stays first on PATH for everything else; only the installs use this one.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          package-manager-cache: false
      - id: corpus-node
        run: echo "dir=$(dirname "$(command -v node)")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # RDT, react-docgen and the oracle run from apps/oracle's dependencies.
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
      # About 10 GB of installed node_modules is too large to cache; the package managers' stores are not.
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .corpora/caches
          key: weekly-${{ hashFiles('scripts/corpora.py', 'pnpm-lock.yaml') }}

1	# Measurement
2	
3	Two things, both small: a weekly record of how Caliper compares with react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and react-docgen on five public repos, and `just bench` for a change that touches the resolver. Nothing here blocks a pull request.
4	
5	## Weekly record
6	
7	`.github/workflows/weekly.yml` runs on Mondays and by hand. `scripts/corpora.py` fetches each repo at a pinned commit and installs its dependencies with its own package manager and lockfile (lifecycle scripts off, caches under `.corpora/`, gitignored), then removes tests, stories, demos and `.d.ts` files from the source directory so every tool reads the same files. `scripts/weekly.py` runs the tools.
8	
9	| Corpus | Repository | Commit | Source directory | Install |
10	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
11	| mantine | `mantinedev/mantine` | `e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d` | `packages/@mantine/core/src` | yarn, immutable |
12	| chakra | `chakra-ui/chakra-ui` | `fa9696f328ea5a0df8685c6d8460edbd779b63b9` | `packages/react/src` | pnpm, frozen |
13	| shadcn | `shadcn-ui/ui` | `ba1503c64472b82256d9de95e2e62c5901a38e8b` | `apps/v4` | pnpm, frozen |
14	| antd | `ant-design/ant-design` | `ba7ccbaa7b4b58ac1ff8e6fe2e78dfa10bfb5538` | `components` | npm, no lockfile (the repo commits none) |
15	| spectrum | `adobe/react-spectrum` | `797762ed3526ea12f089e321bd3891066affad70` | `packages` | yarn, immutable |
16	
17	It records, per corpus and tool, the wall time and peak RSS of one whole run (process start and Node start included), and the size of Caliper's canonical JSON. Caliper runs with `--load-dependencies`; its time is the median of five runs. RDT and react-docgen run once each.
18	
19	Recall is measured against RDT, on the components both tools report (same file, same name):
20	
21	| Measure              | Meaning                                                                                   |
22	| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
23	| Components           | RDT's components with props that the tool also reports                                    |
24	| Own props            | Of those components, RDT's props not declared by `@types/react` that the tool lists       |
25	| `@types/react` props | RDT's props that `@types/react` declares (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `ref`) that the tool lists |
26	
27	react-docgen reads each file alone with its default resolver and importer, as Storybook does, so it lists no types declared elsewhere. That is the point of the comparison.
28	
29	The run uploads `weekly.json` and a table to the job summary. It compares with the last successful run's `weekly.json` and opens, or comments on, one issue labelled `weekly-measurement` when Caliper's time or memory is more than 10% worse, or its recall is more than 2 points lower, on any corpus. There is no committed baseline: the previous run is the baseline.
30	
31	### TypeScript's checker as the oracle
32	
33	RDT has mistakes of its own. With `--oracle` the run also asks TypeScript 7.1's checker (`apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts`, `typescript/sync` of `7.1.0-beta`) for each prop's type and compares it structurally with Caliper's canonical `--json`. The weekly table shows the share of props that agree (identical, or the same type spelled by name) and the share the checker contradicts. This is information only: the checker is a beta and the backend that uses it is an opt-in (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`).
34	
35	| Verdict           | Meaning                                                                          |
36	| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
37	| Identical         | Both sides describe the same type                                                |
38	| Spelled           | The same type, Caliper by name where the checker expands it                      |
39	| Less precise      | Caliper's type is looser or left unevaluated                                     |
40	| Wrong             | Caliper's type describes something else, such as a literal union missing members |
41	| Checker any/error | The checker has no type                                                          |
42	
43	## `just bench`
44	
45	```bash
46	just bench                 # this checkout, uncommitted work included, against origin/main
47	just bench my-branch       # a branch
48	```
49	
50	`scripts/bench.py` builds both in release mode, then times `extract --json` over Mantine and Chakra (source directory only, nothing installed, dependency loading off, no cache) with the two builds interleaved and alternating which goes first. It prints the median wall time and peak RSS of each and their ratio. The first run fetches the two source directories into `.corpora/`.
51	
52	With nothing changed, the ratio stays inside 1.04 for time (95th percentile, 100 trials per corpus on CI and a laptop) and inside 1.12 for memory on CI runners. More than 1.10× in time or 1.20× in memory is worth looking at. Nothing enforces that. Run it before a resolver change goes up for review, and say in the pull request when a cost is intended.
53	
54	## What this replaces
55	
56	Before the weekly record, four workflows (Equivalence, Parity, Scorecard and Allow-list empty) ran against every pull request or `main` push, backed by `scripts/equivalence.py`, a per-pull-request allow-list directory and two committed baselines. They caught one regression in speed and one in output that review would have missed. They also failed on runner noise, on bases that had moved and on their own allow-list, and a lot of one week of merge work went to keeping them green. Git history has them.
57	
58	What we give up: a pull request that slows the resolver or changes output no longer fails by itself. Review, `just bench` and the weekly issue catch it, the last one days later.

- Every missing prop on shadcn and antd is grouped by cause (dependency ComponentProps, Radix/base-ui wrappers, Omit/Pick chains, polymorphic generics, harness pairing) before any fix.
- Own-props recall on shadcn and antd is close to Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum (98.6-99.7%); own props and @types/react props are reported separately.
- Each fix is by shape, not library name, has an exact-content test, and changes no JSON shape after schema v4.
- Each fix passes 'just bench' on time (1.10x) and peak RSS (1.20x).
- Gaps that only the TS checker closes are listed here, not forced into the structural resolver."
mk "Keep readonly, index signatures and RefObject (schema v4)" "One schema bump for syntax the output drops today.

Acceptance:
- readonly, index signatures and RefObject are kept in the output, each with an exact-prop-set test.
- SCHEMA_VERSION is bumped once (3 to 4), readers reject the old version (ADR 0017), and docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md is updated.

mk "Detect components by shape" "Acceptance:
- memo(forwardRef(function ...)) without type arguments is detected, with an exact-content test.
- forwardRef, memo and createContext are matched by import source, not by name.
- The {Name}Props naming heuristic in tagged-factory becomes a shape rule.
- Chakra NonNullable<union> reduces correctly.
- Precision does not regress (docs/precision.md), and time and RSS stay inside bench noise."
mk "Make on-demand TS 7.1 safe to try" "Experimental opt-in only; promotion needs stable TS 7.1 and an oracle wrong-rate near 0%.

Acceptance:
- A supported version range plus a self-check against the installed typescript (it is pinned to 7.1.0-beta today).
- A memory cap for the tsc process (157-612 MiB observed).
- No startup stall; a missing, crashed or slow tsc falls back to the structural answer with one warning (ADR 0022).
- The real-tsc test runs in CI.
- First-story (82-137 ms, Chakra 703) and later-story (21-41 ms) latency re-measured. A disk cache or prefetch only if the numbers justify it."

# Edge cases and known gaps

Gaps that are still open. The 2026-08-04 audit that this file used to record (crash and hang risks, silent data loss, silent wrong output; 43 fixes) has landed; its findings are in git history (`git log --follow docs/edge-cases.md`) and each fix has a regression test. Bugs found by real-library validation are in `rdt-coverage.md`. Type-inference gaps are in `type-checker-integration.md`.

Add an entry when you find a gap you are not fixing now. Delete it when you fix it.

## Detection

- Wrapper calls with no type argument are not recognized: `createIconLoader('x')`, `lazy(() => import(...))`, `createIcon({...})`. Reading the props needs the call's return type, which the structural path doesn't have. The opt-in TypeScript backend (ADR 0006) can.
- Some components are reported under a different name than `react-docgen-typescript` uses: `displayName` assignments, and compound members such as `Tabs.List`.

## Resolution

- Mapped types, conditional types and indexed access over an unbound generic, and `@emotion/styled`'s two-argument overload, need real type inference. They degrade to `Opaque` with a diagnostic and, where possible, a `composes` entry. See `type-checker-integration.md`.
- Ambient globals (`lib.dom.d.ts` and the like) are looked up from `options.src_dirs.first()` only (`pipeline/mod.rs`, `pipeline/revision.rs`). If the first source directory can't resolve `typescript` but a later one could, ambient lookups return nothing for the whole run. Untested against a real multi-root config.

## Output

- TOON is lossy on purpose: unions and intersections print at most 4 members, literal unions at most 6, each followed by `...(+N)`. The module doc of `toon.rs` doesn't say so.
docs/rdt-coverage.md:28:| `array` | **rdt-compat/types** (`string[]` syntax), **day-picker** (`readonly string[]` type-operator form) |
docs/rdt-coverage.md:196:| ✅ done | `readonly X` / `unique X` type operators captured as raw text | now peeled transparently, matching `keyof`'s structured handling |
docs/type-checker-integration.md:7:Slice 1 below covers function components by their export. Next, in order: carry what `PropType` cannot (optional and rest parameters, index signatures, `readonly`), per-prop `tags` and `parent`, class and generic components, `batchRequests` to cut round trips, watch-mode notifications, then the NAPI binding. The client's open Lifecycle items in the Gates table still stand.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:69:- **Not carried:** optional and rest parameters, index signatures, `readonly`, generic parameters of functions, per-prop `tags`, `parent`/`declarations` from the checker. Default exports match by `default` when no export has the component's name.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:206:1. **Output type.** Checker types don't fit `PropType` losslessly: `Named` has no file or symbol, `Tuple` has no optional or rest elements, and `Object` has no index signatures. Add a variant or map into existing ones. `ExtractionOutput` has no schema version, so add one first.
docs/architecture/extractor-ast-visiting.md:52:- **`readonly T[]` and `unique`/`readonly` type operators are peeled transparently, not captured as raw text.** `TSTypeOperatorType::Readonly`/`Unique` unwrap to their operand (mod.rs:512-514) because docgen doesn't track mutability or symbol uniqueness — there's nothing to preserve. Before this, the _entire_ modified type degraded to `CollectedType::Raw`, and downstream heuristics reject any raw string containing a space, so `readonly string[]` (a real `@types/react` `ButtonHTMLAttributes` shape) degraded all the way to `Opaque` even though the element type was fully knowable. `keyof`, by contrast, stays structured (`CollectedType::KeyOf`) because its operand may itself need substitution or resolution later.
docs/architecture/extractor-ast-visiting.md:54:- **Every previously-uncovered type-alias body shape gets a `Passthrough` fallback, not a silent drop.** `classify_type_alias`'s catch-all (alias.rs:236) wraps _anything_ `ts_type_to_collected` can already represent structurally — bare function types, inline object literals, arrays, tuples — in `CollectedTypeAlias::Passthrough`. This replaced a `_ => None` that made the entire alias vanish from `data.type_aliases` with zero diagnostic; every reference to it elsewhere in the file would then resolve as unknown. The dedicated arms above the catch-all (`Omit`, `Pick`, `Partial`, `Required`, `Readonly`, `Union`/`LiteralUnion`, `Intersection`) exist specifically for shapes needing extra alias-specific semantics (Omit's key-splitting, discriminated-union detection) that a transparent passthrough can't express — the catch-all is correct precisely because it only ever runs for shapes with no such semantics.
docs/architecture/extractor-ast-visiting.md:87:- `classify_type_alias`'s `Omit`/`Pick`/`Partial`/`Required`/`Readonly` arms — each malformed-argument early-return (missing type args, wrong arg count, unrecognizable base type) calls `record_skip` before returning `None` (alias.rs, throughout).
docs/architecture/extractor-ast-visiting.md:106:- `classify_type_alias`'s `Omit`/`Pick`/`Partial`/`Required`/`Readonly` arms drop the _entire_ alias on malformed arguments rather than degrading partially (alias.rs) — now diagnosed via `record_skip`, but the alias is still fully absent from `data.type_aliases`.
docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md:39:- **Const arrays:** `(typeof X)[number]` reads `X` as the symbol in scope in the file that wrote the type, project or dependency (`NamedTypeIndex::lookup_const_array`, with the dependency layer as the fallback), then the project's array of that name. An array is an `as const` literal or a `declare const X: readonly ["a", "b"]` annotation, which is how Radix declares `Align` and `Side`.
docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md:151:- **The type of a value built by a call** (`z.infer<typeof schema>` with `const schema = z.object({ ... })`; a store, a hook's result). `typeof X` is a type here only for components, cva variants and `as const` arrays (and now `declare const X: readonly [...]`). TypeScript infers the call's generic arguments from its argument expression and then evaluates the library's conditional and mapped types; that needs the checker (ADR 0006), so the prop stays a named reference (`Event["name"]`) with an Info `OPAQUE_TYPE` diagnostic whose help names the remedy: declare the type where it is used, or `--experimental-semantic-types`. shadcn's `CopyButton.event` is the example.
docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md:9:The canonical JSON (`ExtractionOutput`, `IncrementalUpdate`, the session index) carries `schemaVersion` (ADR 0017); `SCHEMA_VERSION` in `crates/core/src/types/output.rs` is the one definition, and `schema.rs` requires it. Version 1 is the shape ADR 0009 describes. Version 2 (ADR 0018) writes a component's `props` as prop set ids, and an inheritance layer's `omitted` and a diagnostic's `affects` as name list ids, with `propSets` and `nameLists` tables beside `props`. Version 3 adds `optional` and `rest` to a function type's parameters, written only when true, and lists a rest parameter as the last parameter. OXC keeps `...rest` apart from the other parameters and the extractor read only the others, so `(...args: any[]) => void` printed as `() => void` and `(a?: string) => void` as `(a: string) => void`; a caller reading the signature believed an argument was required or that none were accepted. It is a bump, not an addition a reader can ignore: a version 2 reader would show `...args: any[]` as a required parameter named `args`. The Vite plugin and the Storybook addon read version 3 only, and an old parse cache is discarded once. `raw_string` prints `a?: T` and `...a: T[]` as RDT does, TOON prints `T?` and `...T`, and `structural_hash` includes both flags. The TypeScript 7.1 backend does not set them: `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs` builds every parameter as required. Not carried yet, and best landed together as one more bump: `readonly` (the extractor peels it from `readonly string[]` on purpose; carrying it needs a flag on `PropType::Array` and `Tuple`, their collected forms, the union normalizer, the evaluator's assignability and every printer) and `RefObject` (`resolver/react.rs` maps `Ref`, `RefObject`, `ForwardedRef`, `MutableRefObject`, `RefCallback` and `LegacyRef` to one `PropType::Ref { element }`).

import re, sys

for p in sys.argv[1:]:
    s = open(p).read()
    res = ''
    pos = 0
    n = 0
    for m in re.finditer(r'(?<![\w])(?:Collected)?ObjectField \{', s):
        if m.start() < pos:
            continue
        pre = s[max(0, m.start() - 12):m.start()]
        if 'struct' in pre or 'impl' in pre:
            continue
        j = m.end()
        depth = 1
        while depth:
            c = s[j]
            if c == '{':
                depth += 1
            elif c == '}':
                depth -= 1
            j += 1
        body = s[m.end():j - 1]
        if 'description' not in body or 'readonly' in body:
            continue
        res += s[pos:m.end()]
        stripped = body.rstrip()
        tail = body[len(stripped):]
        comma = '' if stripped.endswith(',') else ','
        if '\n' in body:
            indent = re.search(r'\n(\s*)\S', body).group(1)
            res += stripped + comma + f"\n{indent}readonly: false,\n{indent}index_key: None," + tail
        else:
            res += stripped + comma + ' readonly: false, index_key: None' + (tail or ' ')
        res += '}'
        pos = j
        n += 1
    res += s[pos:]

# Unused-dependency check
machete:
    cargo machete

# Mutation testing sweep — slow, run on demand, not part of `just ci`
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi

ts_src := "'packages/vite-plugin/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/storybook/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/storybook/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/storybook/*.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/oracle/src/**/*.ts' 'apps/oracle/tests/**/*.ts'"
ts_src_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/src' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/storybook/src' 'packages/storybook/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/oracle/src'"
ts_tests_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/tests' 'packages/storybook/tests' 'apps/oracle/tests'"
md_src := "'**/*.md' '!node_modules/**' '!target/**' '!dist/**'"

# Lint and format check
lint:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{md_src}}
    pnpm exec oxlint {{ts_src_only}}
    pnpm exec oxlint -A pedantic -A perf -A style -A unicorn/consistent-function-scoping -A vitest/require-mock-type-parameters --vitest-plugin {{ts_tests_only}}

# Format code
fmt:
    cargo fmt
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{md_src}}

# Check licenses, advisories, and banned crates
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Check for typos
typos:
    typos

# Lint GitHub Actions workflows for permission, credential, and supply-chain
# issues. --strict-collection fails on a workflow it cannot parse instead of
# skipping it, so a malformed file can never pass by being ignored.
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Everything the moon-managed pre-commit hook runs. `.moon/workspace.yml`
# calls this recipe rather than repeating the commands, so the hook and
# `just ci` can't drift apart.

input.content:
Prop types now keep three things the output used to drop, in one schema bump (3 to 4):

- `readonly` on arrays, tuples and object fields: `readonly string[]` is no longer `string[]`, and `string[] | readonly string[]` lists both members.
- Index signatures in inline object types: `{ [key: string]: number }` is no longer `{}`.
- The ref type a prop was written with: `RefObject<T>`, `ForwardedRef<T>`, `RefCallback<T>` and the rest no longer all print as `Ref<T>`.

An index signature is not a prop, so everything that reads an object's fields as props, keys or lookup targets skips it (`is_member`). The first draft of this change leaked `key` in as a prop on Chakra and Mantine; `tests/dropped_syntax.rs` pins the exact prop sets so it stays out.

Consumers: `caliper-docgen`, the Vite plugin and the Storybook addon must move together (they reject any other version). The changeset carries the migration note. The parse cache is discarded once (`CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` 27). The TS 7.1 backend sets none of the new fields.

Snapshots: the only changes are `readonly` on `string[]` props in the `@types/react` attributes, `name` on `ref`, and Mantine's `errorProps` keeping its `[key: string]: unknown`.

`just bench` against origin/main, median of 9: Mantine 76 to 79 ms (1.03x), 144 to 144 MiB (1.00x); Chakra 62 to 61 ms (0.99x), 130 to 132 MiB (1.02x). Inside the noise bands.

input.content:
Three of the four detection-by-shape items from trail 127:

- `memo(forwardRef(function Button(props: ButtonProps, ref) {…}))` with no type arguments is now a component with a `ref`; it used to be dropped unless `forwardRef` had two type arguments.
- React's `forwardRef`, `memo` and `createContext` are recognized by where they were imported from (`react`, its subpaths, `preact/compat`), under any alias or namespace (`import { forwardRef as fr }`, `import * as R`). A `forwardRef` imported from another module is not React's, but it still gets its `ref` as before (React Aria's own wrapper), and the generic wrapper conventions still apply to it.
- A tagged factory (`chakra("div", {…})`) takes the props type declared in the file that gives its tag (`interface CenterProps extends HTMLChakraProps<"div">`) instead of whatever is named `{Name}Props`. Factories sharing a tag take the type named for them, and a props type another component already takes is never reused (`StyledGroup`, the private recipe under Chakra's `Group`, would otherwise have claimed `GroupProps`).

Not in this PR: Chakra `NonNullable<union>` reduction. It reduces correctly for local, aliased and inline unions, and Chakra's own source has no unreduced `NonNullable` with dependencies off. The failing case needs a dependency-loaded repro; it stays open on the trail.

Asking the checker for exactly the requested component needs no prediction.
8	
9	`tsc --api` builds its program from the root files it is given and loads what they import. A program rooted at one component's file costs far less than the project, and the process stays up between programs. `crates/semantic/examples/ondemand_bench.rs`, 50 random components per corpus, TypeScript 7.1.0-beta, Apple silicon:
10	
11	| Corpus | First answer | Per component, 1 / 8 / 32 per request | Whole project | Checker peak, one at a time / whole project |
12	| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: |
13	| Mantine | 137 ms | 41 / 6.6 / 2.7 ms | 605 ms | 180 / 276 MiB |
14	| Chakra | 703 ms | 534 / 259 / 108 ms | 9,446 ms | 350 / 972 MiB |
15	| shadcn | 82 ms | 28 / 8.6 / 3.3 ms | 1,518 ms | 157 / 899 MiB |
16	| antd | 91 ms | 37 / 6.1 / 8.4 ms | 489 ms | 612 / 436 MiB |
17	| Spectrum | 131 ms | 21 / 6.5 / 2.2 ms | 618 ms | 218 / 377 MiB |
18	
19	Of a 30 to 40 ms request, 20 to 33 ms builds the program and 2 to 11 ms answers the queries. Initializing the session and parsing the tsconfig once per process, instead of per request, took 10 ms off. For the same components the checker reports 893 props where the structural pass reports 387 on shadcn, 828 against 732 on antd, and the same count on Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum.
20	
21	Through the Storybook harness (`storybook-parity.mjs --variants caliper,caliper-ondemand`, shadcn 95 and antd 83 sampled stories, two runs each, shared machine):
22	
23	| Corpus | Variant    | First story | Median story |     Total |    Peak RSS | Props Storybook lists that we lack |
24	| ------ | ---------- | ----------: | -----------: | --------: | ----------: | ---------------------------------: |
25	| shadcn | structural |   75-144 ms |      2-10 ms | 0.4-1.9 s | 314-324 MiB |                                  0 |
26	| shadcn | on-demand  |  101-335 ms |     29-66 ms | 3.0-7.1 s | 318-328 MiB |                                  0 |
27	| antd   | structural |   59-102 ms |       2-4 ms | 0.2-0.5 s | 222-226 MiB |                                 37 |
28	| antd   | on-demand  |   96-147 ms |     39-53 ms | 3.3-4.6 s | 229-230 MiB |                                  2 |
29	
30	Memory is the addon's; the checker's process is not in the harness figure. With the merge below, shadcn lists every prop Storybook does and antd lacks 2 (`ref`, which the policy omits, and the `capture` attribute, which the curated set does not carry). Default structural mode lacks 37 on antd: `ref`, `capture`, and PurePanel's own and DOM props.
31	
32	## Decision
33	
34	A session can have a checker attached (`WatchSession::with_semantic`, a `SemanticProvider` the semantic crate implements). Core owns the trait and the merge; the checker's process, protocol and threads stay in `caliper-docgen-semantic`, so core does no I/O.
35	
36	- `component(key)` computes the structural answer, asks the checker for that component, and waits up to `semanticWaitMs` (default 150). An answer in time is merged by name: where both have a prop the checker's type, optionality and description win, defaults, tags, `parent` and `declarations` stay structural, and every structural prop the checker did not return stays as the structural pass resolved it. One `Info` provenance diagnostic says so and counts the props kept. A slower checker leaves the structural answer and one `Info` diagnostic saying so; its late answer is kept for the next request.
37	- `htmlAttributes` means the same in both engines, because the checker reports what `@types/react` declares (`children`, `aria-*`, handlers, `className`) flagged `reactDeclared`, never filtered on its side, and the session applies the policy once after the merge (`react_types::checker_prop_used`). `full` takes all of them. `curated` and `none` take only those the structural pass already lists among the component's props (`children` through `PropsWithChildren`, or declared by the component), so the curated attributes and the absence in `none` stay the structural pass's. The request asks only for those names (`SemanticTarget::react_wanted`), so a component does not convert hundreds of DOM attributes it would drop. `key` is omitted in every mode, the one constant that says so being `REACT_SPECIAL_PROPS` in `react_types.rs`. `ref` is a prop (React 19 passes it to function components): `curated` and `full` list it for `ComponentProps<"div">`-style props and for `forwardRef` components, and `none` only when the component declares it.
38	- Answers are cached in memory by component key and the content hash of its file. An edit is a new question.
39	- The checker runs on its own thread with its own runtime, so a caller on any thread can bound its wait. `tsc` starts in the background when the session is created. It is replaced after 64 programs (antd reached 612 MiB after 50) and after a crash; three crashes keep it down for the session.
40	- A missing or unpinned `tsc`, a crash or a timeout yields the structural answer and one `Warning` per session. A request never fails because of the checker.
41	- The option is `semanticTypes: 'off' | 'on-demand'` on the native session and the Storybook addon, with `tscPath` and `semanticWaitMs`. It is off by default and experimental, as ADR 0007 requires.
42	
43	## Consequences
44	
45	- A story gets the checker's props when the checker is warm and answers inside the wait: usually the first story on Mantine, shadcn, antd and Spectrum (82 to 137 ms), and later stories on those at 21 to 41 ms each. That is above the 5 to 20 ms a story can afford, so a story that is not cached takes the structural answer when the checker is busy. Chakra's 534 ms per component never fits the wait; its answer arrives for the next request.
46	- The gain is where the structural pass is behind: shadcn's props more than double. On Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum the checker adds nothing, and the mode only costs a process.
47	- Batching a request to 8 files costs 6 to 9 ms per component (Chakra 259), 32 files 2 to 8 ms (Chakra 108). A prefetch of the components a project's stories name would make most requests cache hits; it is not built here.
48	- The cache is in memory. Reading and writing it under `node_modules/.cache` across runs is the next step, keyed by file hash, tsconfig and lockfile hash, and TypeScript version.
49	- The pin to `7.1.0-beta` stays until TypeScript 7.1 is stable; a version range and a startup `--version` check replace it then.
50	- Peak memory is a `tsc` process of 157 to 612 MiB next to the session. The 64-program replacement bounds it; a memory cap by RSS is not built.
51	
52	## Alternatives considered
53	
54	- One program over the whole project, started in the background. It costs 0.5 to 9.4 s and 276 to 972 MiB, and a single `tsc` answers requests one at a time, so a story would queue behind it.
55	- Route only components a score marks risky. The score measured here catches too few of the components that are wrong (#208) to decide which to send.
56	- Run the checker in the Storybook process. `tsc` is a separate Go binary reached over a pipe; a thread and a runtime of our own keep the session `Send + Sync` without nesting runtimes.
57

- **Fallback:** a missing, unpinned, crashed or timed-out `tsc` gives the structural result plus one `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning, never an error. Per component, the structural result stands for: not exported, class or non-function, overloaded, no props parameter, `any`/`unknown`/generic/union props type, export not found by name (a display name such as `@mantine/core/Accordion` also tries its last segment), or a request the checker rejected. Each is listed with its reason.
- **Tests:** `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` runs the backend against `replay-tsc`, which answers from a recording of the real `7.1.0-beta` (`tests/fixtures/recording.json`, refreshed by `cargo run -p caliper-docgen-semantic --example record_fixture -- <typescript package dir>`); a request the recording lacks fails the test. Fallbacks (no `tsc`, unpinned version, bad path, crash, hang) are asserted as the structural output plus one warning. The CLI test asserts the default output has no `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic.
Measured with `crates/semantic/examples/ondemand_bench.rs` (50 random components, TypeScript 7.1.0-beta): the first answer takes 82 to 137 ms (Chakra 703 ms), a component asked for alone 21 to 41 ms (Chakra 534 ms), and 2 to 9 ms when asked for in batches of 8 to 32. Where the structural pass is behind (shadcn) the checker reports 2.3 times the props; where it is not (Mantine, Chakra, Spectrum) it reports the same count. The in-memory cache, the 64-program process replacement and the failure modes are in the ADR.

## The algorithm

Mirrors RDT 2.4.0 (`lib/parser.js`). Method names are from the 7.1 client.

1. `getSymbolOfSourceFile(file)`, then `getExportsOfModule`.
2. For each export, `getTypeOfSymbol`, then `getSignaturesOfType(Call)`. A component has a signature whose first parameter is named `props` or is the only parameter. For a class, use `Construct` signatures and read `props` from the instance type.
3. Props type: `getTypeOfSymbolAtLocation(param, param.valueDeclaration)`. Props: the type's apparent properties, plus each member's when it is a union.
4. Per prop, `type` is `typeToString(getBaseConstraintOfType(t) ?? t)` with default flags, so long types truncate as they do in RDT. `required` means the symbol lacks `Optional` and has no code default.
5. `parent` is the first declaration's parent when that is an interface or type alias. `declarations` is every declaration's parent.

input.content:
Makes the experimental `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` checker safe to try. It stays off by default and experimental; promotion needs stable TS 7.1 and an oracle wrong-rate near 0%.

- **Version range.** `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` is the `7.1` series (beta, rc, stable) instead of the exact `7.1.0-beta`. A supervisor entry is an exact version or a `major.minor` series (`7.10.0` is not `7.1`). The protocol has no handshake, so the `package.json` version plus the initialize call after the spawn are the self-check; a build failing either gives the structural result and one warning. `PINNED_VERSIONS` is renamed, which is why `caliper-docgen-tsc-client` and `-semantic` get minor bumps.
- **Memory bound.** After every fourth request, once the reply has gone out, the worker reads the `tsc` process's resident memory (`/proc`, else `ps`) and replaces it past `max_rss_mib` (768; single-component programs peak at 157 to 612). Between requests only: one request that needs more finishes first.
- **No stall.** Creating the checker and `warm_up` return at once and a missing `tsc` answers with the structural result (both tested). Dropping the checker used to join the worker, so a request in flight (up to 60 s) blocked closing a session; it now waits at most `shutdown_wait` (5 s) and lets the worker finish alone (tested with the `hang` scenario).
- **CI.** The two tests against the real checker ran only when `CALIPER_TEST_TSC` was set, so never in CI. `test-rust` now points it at `apps/oracle`'s `typescript-beta`, and on CI (`CI` set) a missing variable fails them. They pass locally against 7.1.0-beta (0.9 s and 1.4 s).

Latency re-measured with `ondemand_bench` (30 components, release, 7.1.0-beta): shadcn first answer 84 ms, median 21 ms, p90 37 ms; antd 93 / 36 / 40 ms. ADR 0022 recorded 82 / 28 and 91 / 37, so unchanged; the memory check runs after the reply. No disk cache or prefetch: the numbers do not call for one (first answers are under 100 ms and later ones 21 to 36 ms).

The RSS test needs `ps` or `/proc`; it passes outside the local sandbox and on CI. No JSON shape change.

content.text:
Three PRs are up and ready for review. The shadcn/antd recall fixes (step 3) and the final weekly comparison (step 6) are not done. I need a decision from you on the biggest recall cause before I build those fixes.

- **Step 1, baseline:** I ran the weekly workflow by hand ([run 41159666463](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/actions/runs/41159666463), main `240a61c9`) and recorded the numbers on trail #125. Recall is components / own props / `@types/react` props:

  | Corpus | Components | Own props | `@types/react` props |
  | --- | --: | --: | --: |
  | mantine | 85.9% | 100.0% | 99.2% |
  | chakra | 79.4% | 100.0% | 99.4% |
  | shadcn | 95.2% | 49.7% | 97.1% |
  | antd | 64.0% | 86.4% | 91.9% |
  | spectrum | 76.2% | 99.4% | 98.3% |

  The oracle wrong-rate is 0.00% on all five. The harness reports 1,593 MiB peak RSS for every tool on shadcn, antd and spectrum, which is a measurement artifact I haven't fixed.
- **Step 2, schema v4:** [#266](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/266) bumps `SCHEMA_VERSION` to 4 and keeps `readonly`, index signatures and ref names (`RefObject`, `ForwardedRef`, …). It has exact-prop-set tests in `crates/core/tests/dropped_syntax.rs`, updated serialization docs, and a changeset with the migration note. Bench is within noise: Mantine 1.03× time and 1.00× RSS; Chakra 0.99× and 1.02×.
- **Step 4, detection by shape:** [#267](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/267) covers three of the four items.
  - `memo(forwardRef(fn))` with no type arguments is now detected.
  - React's `forwardRef`, `memo` and `createContext` are matched by import source under any alias.
  - The `{Name}Props` tagged-factory heuristic is now a shape rule: the props type is the one in the file that gives the factory's tag.
  - Component sets and prop names are identical before and after on the Chakra and Mantine sources.
  - The Chakra `NonNullable<union>` item is not done: I could not reproduce it without dependencies loaded, so it stays open on trail #127.
- **Step 5, on-demand hardening:** [#268](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/268).
  - **Version range:** the checker accepts any 7.1 release.
  - **Memory cap:** `tsc` is replaced past 768 MiB between requests.
  - **Shutdown:** dropping the checker no longer waits for a request in progress.
  - **CI:** the real-tsc tests now run there, and a missing `tsc` fails them.
  - **Latency:** first answer 84 ms and median 21 ms on shadcn; 93 ms and 36 ms on antd. That matches ADR 0022, so I built no disk cache or prefetch.

Trails #125–#128 each have acceptance criteria and #126–#128 are linked to their branches. I haven't approved any trail, merged anything or pushed to main. The new commits are GPG-signed.

**Cleanup:** I deleted 142 merged local branches and pruned dead worktrees. Left for you:
- Two agent worktrees with uncommitted files: `agent-a482304b1a114609f` and `agent-a8cdaa39c9352581f`.
- The `scratch/*` worktree and remote branches.
- The other jobs' worktrees under `~/.claude/jobs`.
- The repos at `~/Projects/caliper-homebrew-tap`, `oxc-stack` and `oxc-release-builds`.
- Remote branches and stale Entire trails.
- The root-cause agent's scratch worktree `agent-a9b87f2da7f20385f`.

**What the shadcn/antd gap is:** one cause dominates, and it is a design choice rather than a bug.
- **The cause:** an inherited dependency source over 30 props is collapsed into an inheritance layer (ADR 0012, matching Storybook), and the recall comparison reads only the flat props. With `--collapse-inherited-props none`, shadcn own props go from 49.7% to 91.1% and antd from 86.4% to 99.3%.
- **antd PurePanel:** it is this same collapse, not a pairing bug.
- **Structural fixes:** none need the TS checker and none change the JSON shape. They are terminal React builtins (`AriaAttributes`, `HTMLProps`, `RefAttributes`), module augmentation of `HTMLAttributes` (`tw`), `Pick<…, keyof …>` and union props, object-literal components, and `key`.

needs input: should the recall comparison count collapsed inheritance layers, or should `--format rdt` stop collapsing? I'd lean toward the first, since the collapse is deliberate and Storybook-compatible. Once you decide I'll build the structural fixes as separate small PRs, and I'll re-run the weekly workflow after #266–#268 merge so step 6 compares against the baseline.
